alerts.title: Rising creatinine on TDF during pregnancy
alerts.message: TDF is associated with nephrotoxicity including elevated creatinine. Patient's creatinine rose from 0.8 to 1.1 mg/dL (37.5% increase) within 10 weeks of starting TDF/3TC/DTG, and eGFR is now 78 mL/min/1.73m². DTG can also cause a small creatinine increase via inhibition of tubular secretion. Pregnancy normally increases GFR, so creatinine should trend downward, making this rise more concerning. However, the absolute creatinine of 1.1 remains within normal range, and phosphate is normal at 3.8 mg/dL, arguing against significant proximal tubular dysfunction. Urinalysis is normal with no proteinuria. Continued monitoring is warranted given the combined TDF + DTG exposure in pregnancy.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat creatinine and eGFR at next visit. If creatinine continues rising or eGFR declines further, consider TDF substitution. Monitor phosphate and urinalysis.

alerts.title: DTG and iron supplement interaction in pregnancy
alerts.message: DTG absorption is reduced by divalent cations including iron. Patient is taking ferrous sulfate and folic acid as prescribed during pregnancy. Guidelines note the interaction between DTG and divalent cation-containing medications in pregnancy, as pregnant women frequently receive iron or calcium supplements. This interaction may reduce DTG levels and compromise viral suppression. However, the patient's viral load has already declined from 125,000 to 89 copies/mL after 10 weeks, suggesting current absorption is adequate. Separating DTG and iron dosing by at least 2 hours (or taking iron with food and DTG on an empty stomach) minimises this interaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel patient to separate DTG and ferrous sulfate dosing by at least 2 hours. Verify at next visit that viral load remains suppressed.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring frequency in pregnancy
alerts.message: Guidelines specify viral load monitoring at 3 months for pregnant women newly initiating ART. Patient's VL at 10 weeks (89 copies/mL) aligns with this schedule and confirms suppression. Guidelines also indicate repeat VL at delivery if gestation exceeds 28 weeks at the time of the 3-month VL. At 22 weeks pregnant with VL done at ~10 weeks post-initiation, a repeat VL at delivery is indicated. Additionally, guidelines state VL monitoring at 6 months after ART initiation and every 6-12 months thereafter. No clinician plan was documented today, so it is unclear if follow-up VL timing was addressed.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule repeat viral load at delivery (patient will be >28 weeks). Continue routine VL monitoring at 6 months post-ART initiation and every 6-12 months thereafter.

alerts.title: No clinician assessment or plan documented
alerts.message: No clinician assessment or plan was documented for this visit. The patient is a pregnant woman on ART for 10 weeks with rising creatinine, a DTG-iron supplement interaction to manage, and specific VL monitoring requirements in pregnancy. Guidelines require structured follow-up including VL monitoring at delivery and ongoing renal monitoring on TDF. The absence of a documented plan risks gaps in managing these issues. Weight gain of 6 kg (62 to 68 kg) since pre-pregnancy may reflect normal pregnancy progression but should be assessed alongside DTG-associated weight gain.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment and plan addressing renal monitoring, DTG-iron separation, VL at delivery, and weight trend. Schedule next antenatal ART follow-up.
